run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: I fetched the runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook and carried out its steps with my own tools. Step 1 (signup status/describe/logs): both signup-service pods in namespace app-162 (signup-service-7c89545dc9-762tw and signup-service-7c89545dc9-9kzmt) are Running with restartCount 0 but Ready=False/ContainersNotReady, and their logs repeat 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' immediately followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503'. Step 2 (payments health): payments-service-6d94c44fdc-jmkfv is Running, not Ready, restartCount 0, and logs 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' plus 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' with /health and /ready returning 503; a Warning Unhealthy event records 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503'; the payments-service Deployment reports Available=False / MinimumReplicasUnavailable. Step 3 (service-to-service reachability): I could not exec into a pod (no exec tool); instead the Endpoints object for Service payments-service contains only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.49) and no ready addresses, which explains signup's connection refused. Step 4 (payments-specific issues): the Stripe key failure is present in the pod's own logs; no database/Postgres error lines appeared in the payments or signup logs I read. Step 5 (environment variables): I read the env wiring from the Deployment specs - STRIPE_API_KEY comes from secretKeyRef payments-secrets/stripe-api-key and DATABASE_URL from payments-secrets/database-url (signup from signup-secrets) - but secret values cannot be read, so the stored key value itself was not verified. The deepest supported cause is that invalid Stripe API key: it keeps payments-service unready (no ready Service endpoints), and signup-service's own readiness check of that dependency returns 503, so signup pods never become Ready. No NetworkPolicy, Ingress or ResourceQuota exists in the cluster, both Deployments are at revision 1 with ReplicaSets created at 16:59:20Z and containers with restartCount 0, so this is not a rollout, crash loop, eviction/OOM or network-policy problem. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for every query in this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, latency or trace confirmation exists, the actual secret value could not be read, change history is not integrated, and no registration request was observed in the logs, so end-user registration failures are unverified rather than measured.

claims.text: payments-service container log at 2026-11-23T16:59:22Z states 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', and at 16:59:30Z 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' while GET /health and GET /ready returned 503.

Deployment payments-service in namespace app-162 injects STRIPE_API_KEY into the container from secretKeyRef name payments-secrets key stripe-api-key (and DATABASE_URL from key database-url), with readiness probe HTTP GET /ready:8080 and liveness probe HTTP GET /health:8080.

Pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-jmkfv (namespace app-162, created 2026-11-23T16:59:20Z, owned by ReplicaSet payments-service-6d94c44fdc) is phase Running but condition Ready=False and ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady, container restartCount 0, no lastState termination.

Deployment payments-service status condition is Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable and message 'Deployment does not have minimum availability.'; its Progressing condition is ReplicaSetUpdated.
A Warning event (count 2) on Pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-jmkfv at 2026-11-23T16:59:40Z records 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503'.

Endpoints object for Service payments-service (namespace app-162) lists only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.49, pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-jmkfv, port 8080) and no ready addresses, while the Service selector app=payments-service matches that pod.

Both signup-service pods (signup-service-7c89545dc9-762tw and signup-service-7c89545dc9-9kzmt, created 2026-11-23T16:59:20Z, owner ReplicaSet signup-service-7c89545dc9) are Running with restartCount 0 but Ready=False/ContainersNotReady; the Endpoints object for Service signup-service has only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.47, 10.244.0.48).

signup-service pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-762tw logs '2026-11-23 16:59:26/31/36 - ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' each followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503 -'; the container has no previous instance.

signup-service pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-9kzmt shows the same repeating pattern from 16:59:26Z to 16:59:36Z: 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503 -'.

Deployment signup-service in app-162 sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080, keys readiness on HTTP GET /ready:8080, and its status condition is Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable.

Only two ReplicaSets exist in app-162, payments-service-6d94c44fdc and signup-service-7c89545dc9, both created 2026-11-23T16:59:20Z, owned by their Deployments, and both Deployments carry deployment.kubernetes.io/revision "1" with a kubectl-client-side-apply managed-fields entry at 16:59:20Z; events show Deployment ScalingReplicaSet from 0 to 1 (payments) and 0 to 2 (signup) at 16:59:20Z.
Querying all namespaces returned no NetworkPolicy objects, no Ingress objects and no ResourceQuota objects at query time.

All 24 otel-demo/kube-system/local-path-storage Deployments returned by the cluster-wide Deployment query have availableReplicas equal to replicas (e.g. payment 1/1, checkout 1/1, frontend 1/1), while payments-service and signup-service in app-162 show readyReplicas and availableReplicas null.

A NetworkPolicy blocking signup-service from reaching payments-service is rejected: no NetworkPolicy objects exist anywhere in the cluster, and the payments Endpoints object shows the pod matched the Service selector but sat in notReadyAddresses, which explains the connection refused without any policy.

A crash/restart, OOMKill or eviction of the signup or payments pods is rejected: all three app-162 pods have restartCount 0, no lastState termination and no OOMKilled/Evicted event; the only events are Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/SuccessfulCreate/ScalingReplicaSet plus one Warning Unhealthy liveness 503.

flagd fault injection is rejected as the cause here: the flagd-config ConfigMap (namespace otel-demo) has paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable with defaultVariant "off", and the app-162 Deployments reference no flagd sidecar or flag environment, only PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL, DATABASE_URL, STRIPE_API_KEY and PORT.

A configuration rollout or restart with an unchanged pod template is rejected as the trigger: each app-162 Deployment has exactly one ReplicaSet at revision 1, created together with the pods at 16:59:20Z by kubectl-client-side-apply, with no SuccessfulDelete events and restartCount 0, i.e. an initial scale-up rather than a replacement.

The invalid Stripe API key most likely lives in Secret app-162/payments-secrets under key stripe-api-key, since that is the only source wired into the failing STRIPE_API_KEY variable; the secret's value could not be read, so this is an inference from the Deployment env wiring plus the service's own 'invalid test key' log.

A second, independent cause could exist in the database dependency (DATABASE_URL sourced from payments-secrets/database-url and signup-secrets/database-url): no database or Postgres error line appeared in the payments or signup logs read, but the URLs are unreadable secrets and payments' readiness is gated on the Stripe key first, so a DB fault cannot be excluded.

End-user registration failures are plausibly caused by signup pods never being Ready (no ready Service endpoints, /ready 503 on the dependency check), but no /register request or its error was observed in the sampled logs, so actual request-level registration impact remains unverified.

Verify and correct the value of key stripe-api-key in Secret app-162/payments-secrets with a valid Stripe key (requires secret read/write permission this Run does not have), then roll the payments-service Deployment and confirm /health and /ready return 200 before checking that signup /ready turns 200.

Make signup-service resilient to a broken payments dependency (circuit breaker/retry and a readiness check that distinguishes 'dependency down' from 'self unhealthy' where that is safe), and alert directly on payments-service /ready 503 and Deployment Available=False rather than only on signup symptoms.

gaps: Secrets cannot be read in this Run: the actual value of app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key (and database-url), and the 'app-code' secret volume contents, were not verified; the invalid-key conclusion rests on the payments-service pod's own log plus the Deployment env wiring.

Prometheus was unavailable for every query attempted in this Run (get_metric_names and execute_prometheus_instant_query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, latency or up-series reading exists for app-162 signup-service/payments-service; a missing series is unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable for every query attempted (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there are no spans to confirm the signup to payments call edge or any baseline/incident latency comparison.
The change_history integration is listed as not_integrated, so who changed the Stripe key/secret and when could not be determined, and the declared fault itself was never observed happening.
No /register (or any registration) request appears in the signup-service log lines read, so request-level registration failures and customer impact are unverified.
I could not carry out runbook step 3 as written (kubectl exec / port-forward) because no exec tool is available; the reachability conclusion comes from the Endpoints object instead.

Only 3 events fell outside the authorized window and were dropped, and container 'previous' log instances did not exist, so nothing before 2026-11-23T16:59:20Z (when both workloads were first scaled up) is observable.
next_steps: With secret access, print and validate the stripe-api-key value referenced by Deployment payments-service (secret payments-secrets, key stripe-api-key) and compare it with a known-valid Stripe test key.
Also verify the database-url values behind payments-secrets and signup-secrets, since a DB failure is not yet excluded.
Run the runbook's reachability test from inside a signup pod (curl -v http://payments-service:8080/health) once payments has ready endpoints, to confirm the connection-refused symptom clears.
After correcting the key, confirm payments-service pods reach Ready=True, Endpoints for payments-service shows ready addresses, and signup-service /ready returns 200 on both replicas.
Add or verify a Prometheus/Jaeger path for the app-162 services so readiness 503s and dependency failures are alertable rather than detectable only from pod logs.

    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
